annotation.title_clean: Can robots be trustworthy? Reflections about responsive robots and trust as a human capability
annotation.title_en: Can robots be trustworthy? Reflections about responsive robots and trust as a human capability
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Schröder, I.; Müller, O.; Scholl, H.; Levy-Tzedek, S.; Kellmeyer, P.
annotation.summary_en: Philosophical article critiquing the conceptualisation of trust and trustworthiness for social care robots, including in the EU High-Level Expert Group on AI guidelines. It argues trust is a responsive human capability and that robots' constructed responsiveness cannot meet its ethical demands, so robots should not be designed to be overly trust-inciting.
key_provisions_or_claims: Trust is a human capability that is fundamentally responsive and needs responsive others.
Treating trustworthiness as a measurable design feature is philosophically insufficient.
Social robots only simulate responsivity, so their ability to meet the ethical demands of care is limited.
Care robots should not be designed to be too trust-inciting.
The EU HLEG trustworthy-AI concept of trust is critically examined.
